I am 65 years old and have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I know this land, and the wheat-maize rotation is what works here on the North China Plain. With six people in my household and some family members working off-farm, I have enough labor for the busy seasons, but I must keep my management practical and reliable—I cannot afford to gamble on fancy new methods.

For this year's winter wheat, I will rotary till the entire 10.1 mu before sowing in October. I will plant an improved wheat variety from the county supply station—not traditional seed, but one I have used for years and trust. I have well irrigation, so I will irrigate four times: at sowing if the soil is dry, once before winter to protect the seedlings, again at the jointing stage in spring, and a final time during grain filling. For fertilizer, I will apply compound fertilizer as a base and topdress with urea in spring, using about 18 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I will spray pesticides three times: a herbicide at sowing, and then fungicide or insecticide in spring if the weather brings disease or pests. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on the same 10.1 mu. Time is short between crops, so I will use no-tillage seeding directly into the wheat stubble to save time and preserve soil moisture. I will irrigate three times—at sowing if needed, at the big trumpet stage, and during flowering and grain filling. I will apply about 16 kg of nitrogen, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu, mostly as base and one topdressing. I will spray herbicide at sowing and watch for corn borer and aphids, applying pesticide twice total. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

This is my plan. I have done this for decades. I watch the sky and adjust, but this is my foundation.
